title: 1664-expectation-propagation-dynamic-probit
universal_lens: Expectation propagation (EP) approximates dynamic probit smoothing distributions via Gaussian site updates, leveraging moment-matching and Kalman-style passes for state dynamics. Expectation propagation (EP) approximates posterior distributions in dynamic probit models via moment matching, offering speed at cost of convergence guarantees.
gsi_mapping: EP enables Bayesian inference over latent states in dynamic binary models, supporting conformal predictive distributions for probabilistic forecasting in GSI's uncertainty quantification framework. GSI employs EP for Bayesian inference on binary event probabilities, leveraging conformal prediction for calibrated uncertainty quantification in real-time sports analytics.
gse_mapping: EP supports GSE's state-transition reasoning by providing fast, approximate smoothing distributions that enable real-time situational awareness under stochastic binary outcomes. GSE integrates EP as a fast approximate inference engine within its state-space framework, enabling rapid policy updates and situational reasoning during live game dynamics.

primitives.name: EP Smoothing Approximation
primitives.verbatim_quote: EP approximates the SUN smoothing distribution by a Gaussian, iteratively refining site approximations: each likelihood factor's contribution is matched by moment-matching (mean and covariance) against the tilted distribution.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta': 'latent state vector, dimensionless', '\\mathbf{m}': 'mean vector of Gaussian approximation, same units as \\theta', '\\mathbf{V}': 'covariance matrix of Gaussian approximation, squared units of \\theta'}
primitives.assumptions: Posterior is unimodal and well-approximated by a Gaussian; EP fixed-point convergence not guaranteed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When posterior becomes multimodal or heavy-tailed, Gaussian approximation fails.

layer2.mapping: EP's moment-matching procedure mirrors GSI's variational inference isomorphism, where site approximations correspond to belief updates in Bayesian networks.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between true SUN and EP Gaussian approximation.

primitives.name: Site Update Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Site updates: for each t, cavity q_{\t}(θ_t) ∝ q(θ_t)/q̃_t(θ_t); tilted p̂ ∝ q_{\t} · p(y_t|θ_t); moment-match E_{p̂}[θ_t], Cov_{p̂}[θ_t] to update site q̃_t.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{q}_{\\setminus t}(\\theta_t)': 'cavity distribution, dimensionless', '\\tilde{q}_t(\\theta_t)': 'current site approximation, dimensionless', '\\hat{p}': 'tilted distribution, dimensionless', 'E_{\\hat{p}}[\\theta_t]': 'expected value of \\theta_t under \\hat{p}, same units as \\theta_t', 'Cov_{\\hat{p}}[\\theta_t]': 'covariance of \\theta_t under \\hat{p}, squared units of \\theta_t'}
primitives.assumptions: Closed-form tilted moments exist via truncated normal formulas; iterative refinement converges.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When truncated normal moments cannot be computed analytically, numerical integration required.

layer2.mapping: The site update kernel in EP corresponds to GSE's belief propagation kernel, where local evidence is combined with global beliefs through moment-matching.
layer2.telemetry: Change in site approximation across iterations (residual norm).

primitives.name: Kalman Smoother Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: - State dynamics handled by Kalman-smoother-style forward-backward passes within each EP sweep.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbf{F}_t': 'forward filtered estimate, same units as \\theta_t', '\\mathbf{B}_t': 'backward smoothed estimate, same units as \\theta_t'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear-Gaussian state dynamics; Kalman filter provides sufficient statistics for smoothing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Nonlinear or non-Gaussian dynamics invalidate standard Kalman smoother.

layer2.mapping: Integration of Kalman smoother into EP allows GSE to handle temporal dependencies in latent states efficiently.
layer2.telemetry: Smoothing error relative to exact MCMC or PFM-VB estimates.

primitives.name: Probabilistic Model Setup
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method/model Same dynamic probit setup as 1661: y_t ∈ {0,1}, P(y_t=1)=Φ(x_t'θ_t), θ_t = θ_{t-1}+η_t.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_t': 'binary outcome, dimensionless', 'x_t': 'regression vector, dimensionless', '\\theta_t': 'latent state, dimensionless', '\\eta_t': 'state noise, same units as \\theta_t'}
primitives.assumptions: Probit link function; Gaussian noise in state evolution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observation or state models deviate from Bernoulli/probit structure.

layer2.mapping: This setup mirrors GSI’s binary outcome modeling, enabling direct application of EP to GSE's dynamic inference tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of predicted probabilities vs empirical frequencies.

primitives.assumptions: Model assumes static latent variables and fixed hyperparameters; convergence not guaranteed without damping.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model complexity exceeds computational limits or when convergence fails under standard EP updates.

reasoning_traces.think:
The chapter introduces expectation propagation (EP) as a method for approximating the smoothing distribution in a dynamic probit model. The core idea is to iteratively refine Gaussian approximations to the true posterior using moment-matching against tilted distributions derived from individual likelihood factors. This approach leverages the structure of the probit model—where observations are binary and governed by a latent linear dynamical system—to perform efficient inference. The key innovation lies in combining EP with Kalman-smoother-style passes to handle the temporal dependencies in the latent states. The method assumes a unimodal posterior and that the Gaussian approximation is adequate, which may break down in complex or multimodal settings. The evaluation uses CAC40 data, demonstrating EP's ability to match performance with other methods like PFM-VB and exact MCMC, though at the cost of theoretical convergence guarantees. From a GSI perspective, this represents a viable backend for probabilistic forecasting in binary time series. For GSE, it offers a computationally efficient way to reason about evolving states under uncertain binary outcomes, particularly useful in real-time strategic decision-making scenarios. The core contribution lies in demonstrating that while EP offers substantial speedups (~100×) over exact inference, it incurs only marginal accuracy improvements over PFM-VB. The lack of convergence guarantees and absence of public code underscore the practical challenges in deploying EP reliably.
